Osteoporosis Overview

Osteoporosis • A systemic metabolic • disease of bone that leads to a reduction in bone mineral density (BMD) • Affected bones become thinner, more likely to break (fractures) that may result in pain & other complications, including loss of independence • “Silent disease” - most people don’t know they have osteoporosis until they suffer a broken bone from a minor fall or bump 12/9/2025

Osteoporosis Overview

Osteoporosis • A systemic metabolic • disease of bone that leads to a reduction in bone mineral density (BMD) • Affected bones become thinner, more likely to break (fractures) that may result in pain & other complications, including loss of independence • “Silent disease” - most people don’t know they have osteoporosis until they suffer a broken bone from a minor fall or bump 12/9/2025

With broken skin, risk of infection due to bacteria & other contaminants entering wound. Early treatment focuses on preventing infection The wound, tissues & bone must be cleaned out in surgical procedures as soon as possible. Fractured bone would be stabilized with a surgical procedure to allow wound healing.

Osteoporosis Overview

Osteoporosis • A systemic metabolic • disease of bone that leads to a reduction in bone mineral density (BMD) • Affected bones become thinner, more likely to break (fractures) that may result in pain & other complications, including loss of independence • “Silent disease” - most people don’t know they have osteoporosis until they suffer a broken bone from a minor fall or bump 12/9/2025

Osteoporosis Overview

Osteoporosis • A systemic metabolic • disease of bone that leads to a reduction in bone mineral density (BMD) • Affected bones become thinner, more likely to break (fractures) that may result in pain & other complications, including loss of independence • “Silent disease” - most people don’t know they have osteoporosis until they suffer a broken bone from a minor fall or bump 12/9/2025

Compound fracture a fracture with an open wound/ skin breaks near the site of broken bone. Usually caused by a fragment of bone breaking through the skin during injury. With broken skin, risk of infection due to bacteria & other contaminants entering wound. Early treatment focuses on preventing infection The wound, tissues & bone must be cleaned out in surgical procedures as soon as possible. Fractured bone would be stabilized with a surgical procedure to allow wound healing.

summary_units.title: Arthritis Overview
summary_units.summary: Arthritis Latin word: ➢ arthron – Joint ➢ itis – Inflammation ➢ very common but NOT ➢ well understood ➢ NOT a single disease ➢ informal way of referring ➢ to joint pain/joint disease ➢ > 100 different types of arthritis & related conditions 1/9/2025 Common signs & symptoms Joint swelling, pain, ➢ stiffness & decreased range of motion (ROM) ➢ may last for years, ➢ progress/get worse with ➢ time ➢ mild, moderate or severe ➢ may result in chronic pain, ➢ inability to do daily activities, difficulty in walking (both level ground / stairs) 1/9/2025 Common signs & symptoms • may cause permanent joint deformity (changes in shape) • some are visible, such as knobby finger joints, but often only be seen on X- • ray • some types of arthritis also affect other areas like heart, eyes, lungs, kidneys & skin 1/9/2025 Diagnosis Subjectiveexamination - onset, • pattern, means to relieve Objectiveexamination: • Acute inflammation: • Redness, jointswelling, • warmth& pain • Joint crepitus: clicking/popping • “Locking”/“sticking” during • movement • Range of motion (active, assisted, • passive) • Joint instability with muscle • weakness/buckling Imaging test: X-ray • 1/9/2025

summary_units.title: Stages of OA Knee
summary_units.summary: Stage of Osteoarthritis Knee Stage 1: Minor • slight damage to cartilage +/- • osteophytes • NO apparent narrowing of joint space • (normal at X-ray) • Asymptomatic (NO pain / discomfort) Stage 2: Mild • some symptoms noted like • joint stiffness & pain, esp. after prolonged sitting • X-ray:clearly shown growth • of osteophytes, cartilage begin to get thin 1/9/2025 Stage of Osteoarthritis Knee Stage 3: Moderate • moderate narrow joint space, with cartilage loss • thickening of bone just • underneath cartilage • pain & discomfort with daily activities like • walking, bending • joint inflammation - excess synovial fluid • increase swelling 1/9/2025 Stage of Osteoarthritis Knee Stage 4: Severe • further joint space • narrowing, with continuous cartilage loss • more significant pain & discomfort with daily activities due to joint • friction • X-ray: bone on bone • (cartilage completely worn / little left) • Deformity with varus (bow leg) or valgus (knock knee) 1/9/2025

summary_units.title: Common Joint Deformities in RA
summary_units.summary: Common Joint Deformities in RA Ulnar drift Claw toes C1-C2 subluxation Boutonniere Deformity Swan Neck Deformity 1/9/2025 Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) • Recommend early • diagnosis with aggressive treatment • most commonly affects joints of the hands, feet, wrists, elbows, knees and ankles • usually symmetrical • Can affect body systems, • such as skin, eyes, cardiovascular or respiratory systems • Can cause long-term • disability, pain & premature death 1/9/2025 Signs & symptoms – Joints • Joint pain, tenderness, swelling, redness or stiffness > 6 weeks • Morning stiffness for > 1 hour • > ONE joint are affected • Small joints are commonly • affected – Hands, Wrists & toes • Symmetrical joint pain: on both sides of the body • Decrease joint range of • motion (ROM) • Joint deformity Flare - a period of high disease activity, last for days/months ** increases in inflammation & other symptoms 1/9/2025 Signs & symptoms – organs & body systems • Whole body: fatigue, loss of appetite & low-grade fever • Lungs: chest pain, shortness of breath (SOB), persistent cough - • inflammation & scarring • Heart: chest pain - inflammation of • tissue around the heart • Eyes: dryness, pain, redness • Blood vessels: affect blood flow • Skin: rheumatoid nodules – small lumps under the skin over bony • areas • Nerve: numbness, tingling, pain, • weakness • Blood: anaemia, low RBC • Bone: Osteoporosis • Mouth: dryness and gum problems 1/9/2025

summary_units.title: Ankylosing Spondylitis
summary_units.summary: Ankylosing Spondylitis (AS) • Relative uncommon rheumatic disease that affect the spine • Prevalence: • Global – 0.1-1.4% [Dean et al, 2014] [Dean et al, 2014] • Hong Kong – 0.2-0.3% [Zhu et al, 2008] [Zhu et al, 2008] • long-term condition related to autoimmune disease • Joints and ligaments of spine and other areas of the body become • inflamed • e.g. sacroiliac joint, hips, • shoulders • May involve other organs such as eyes, lungs, heart 1/9/2025 Signs & symptoms • Symptoms tend to develop gradually (over several months or years) • Morning stiffness > 30 min • Symptoms may come and go over time (flare) • Varies in symptoms, including pain, stiffness & swelling over back, sacroiliac joint, hips and • shoulders • extreme tiredness (fatigue) • For severe cases, vertebrae fuse together lead to rigid spine 1/9/2025 Ankylosing Spondylitis (AS) Causes: • no known cause • link with a particular gene variant known as HLA-B27 Risk factors: • Family history and genetics • Age (usually symptoms develop before age 45) • Biological gender: male • Autoimmune disease: psoriasis, Crohn’s disease, ulcerative colitis 1/9/2025 Ankylosing Spondylitis (AS) Treatment: • No cure for AS, treatment • available to relieve the symptoms and delay • progression • Medications to reduce pain & • inflammation: • NSAIDS • DMARDs, Biologics • Corticosteriods • Exercises: reduce pain & • stiffness • Physiotherapy: improve posture, • flexibility, joint mobility • Surgery: for rare cases to repair significantly damaged joints or correct severe bends in spine 1/9/2025

summary_units.title: Osteoporosis Overview
summary_units.summary: Osteoporosis • A systemic metabolic • disease of bone that leads to a reduction in bone mineral density (BMD) • Affected bones become thinner, more likely to break (fractures) that may result in pain & other complications, including loss of independence • “Silent disease” - most people don’t know they have osteoporosis until they suffer a broken bone from a minor fall or bump 12/9/2025 Osteoporosis & Bone Remodeling • Bone remodeling - continuous process throughout life to maintaining bone strength and repairing micro-damage • Osteoporosis is the imbalance between bone resorption (breakdown) by osteoclasts and bone formation (building) by osteoblasts, leading to a net bone loss (Chang et al, 2019) 12/9/2025 Disease Progression Severe Normal Bone Osteopenia Osteoporosis Osteoporosis Osteoporosis - causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment, pathology https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6fMkX1J9gWw https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ge58qnQMBJY 12/9/2025 Changes in Bone Mass with Age in Male/Female Later life (50-65 yrs) Elderly life (65 onwards) Early Adulthood (up to Middle Age (30s-50s) 30s) Bone loss sharply ↑, esp. for women during & Both men and women Bone breakdown > bone after menopause.

summary_units.title: Types
summary_units.summary: Open/Close Fracture Open (or compound) • A fracture in which at least one end of the broken bone tears through the skin; carries a high risk of infection Closed (or simple) • A fracture in which the skin remains intact 12/9/2025 Displaced/Non-displaced Fracture Non-displaced (stable) fractures • fracture ends are aligned Displaced (unstable) • fractures • fracture ends are separated or misaligned 12/9/2025 Complete Fracture Complete fractures extend across the whole bone • Transverse: straight across the long axis of the bone • Oblique: at an • angle that is not 90° • Spiral: as a result of a twisting motion • Comminuted: many small pieces between two large segments 12/9/2025 Incomplete Fracture Incomplete fractures does NOT extend across the whole bone/partial fracture • Greenstick: partial fracture with one side of the bone broken, often occurs in children • Hairline: microscopic fracture often due to repeated stress 12/9/2025

summary_units.title: Osteoporosis Overview
summary_units.summary: Osteoporosis • A systemic metabolic • disease of bone that leads to a reduction in bone mineral density (BMD) • Affected bones become thinner, more likely to break (fractures) that may result in pain & other complications, including loss of independence • “Silent disease” - most people don’t know they have osteoporosis until they suffer a broken bone from a minor fall or bump 12/9/2025 Osteoporosis & Bone Remodeling • Bone remodeling - continuous process throughout life to maintaining bone strength and repairing micro-damage • Osteoporosis is the imbalance between bone resorption (breakdown) by osteoclasts and bone formation (building) by osteoblasts, leading to a net bone loss (Chang et al, 2019) 12/9/2025 Disease Progression Severe Normal Bone Osteopenia Osteoporosis Osteoporosis Osteoporosis - causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment, pathology https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6fMkX1J9gWw https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ge58qnQMBJY 12/9/2025 Changes in Bone Mass with Age in Male/Female Later life (50-65 yrs) Elderly life (65 onwards) Early Adulthood (up to Middle Age (30s-50s) 30s) Bone loss sharply ↑, esp. for women during & Both men and women Bone breakdown > bone after menopause.

summary_units.title: Lecture 2 - Bone problems: osteoporosis, fracture and amputation
summary_units.summary: HAS4185J L2: Orthopaedic – Bone Problems: Osteoporosis, Fracture, Amputation Bones Functions of bones • Protects internal • organs (e.g. brain, spinal cord, heart, lung) • Stores and releases (e.g. Calcium, fat) • Support – like a scaffold • Movement – for attachment of • muscles & tendons • Produces blood cells – in bone marrow 12/9/2025 Histology of Bone Periosteum • Outer most fibrous layer • Dense - extra protection, • strength & durability • Contains blood vessels, nerves • and lymphatic vessels • Bone grow, repair, remodeling • Joint cartilage • at epiphyses (2 ends of the bone) • Hyaline cartilage • Reduces friction and act as • shock absorber 12/9/2025 Compact & Spongy Bone Compact (Cortical) bone • Hard outer layer of all bones • Dense and strong • Protective layer of inner cavity • & provides strength for bone Spongy (Cancellous) Bone • Spongy inner layer network of • trabeculae • Lighter and less dense • More spaces in some spongy • bones contain red bone marrow ALL bones are composed of life tissues with combination of Compact et al., 2017) & Cancellous bone, this depends on • Size • Shape • Functions • 12/9/2025 Osteoporosis • A systemic metabolic • disease of bone that leads to a reduction in bone mineral density (BMD) • Affected bones become thinner, more likely to break (fractures) that may result in pain & other complications, including loss of independence • “Silent disease” - most people don’t know they have osteoporosis until they suffer a broken bone from a minor fall or bump 12/9/2025 Osteoporosis & Bone Remodeling • Bone remodeling - continuous process throughout life to maintaining bone strength and repairing micro-damage • Osteoporosis is the imbalance between bone resorption (breakdown) by osteoclasts and bone formation (building) by osteoblasts, leading to a net bone loss (Chang et al, 2019) 12/9/2025
